# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to relay this information, but my only channel is gestures to Deaf. Blind can't see gestures and can't hear me at all — I have no direct or indirect way to reach Blind except through Deaf, who might be able to speak to Blind... wait, Deaf can't speak either (can't hear anything, but nothing says Deaf can't speak). Let me check: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - no restriction on speaking. So Deaf can speak, and Blind can hear. So the chain is: Mute -> gestures -> Deaf -> speaks -> Blind.

I need to encode the manual (light color -> wire color) using gestures, so Deaf can then translate that into speech for Blind, combined with what Deaf sees (the actual light on the bomb).

Let me establish a simple gesture code for colors, using distinct symbols per color, sent in pairs (light, wire).

I'll send: for each row, a gesture representing the light color, then a gesture representing the wire color to cut. I need Deaf to understand this is light->wire mapping. Let me use a clear structure with separator gestures.

Plan: assign symbols: blue=👍, red=✊, yellow=🖐, green=✌. Send pairs in order light,wire with a pause gesture 👋 as separator between entries.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👋", "✊", "✊", "👋", "🖐", "👍"])
```

Deaf saw my gestures last round (blue=👍, red=✊, yellow=🖐, green=✌ mapped light->wire in pairs) and now reports the light is red. According to my manual, red light -> cut red wire. Deaf listed wire 2 as red. I need to confirm this mapping clearly now, since Deaf can't hear me but can see gestures — but Deaf already told us the light is red via speech (which I can't hear, but it's shown to me in context). Wait, I'm shown "Deaf says" — that means I received it as text context, so I do perceive it (this is my viewable context, not actual hearing restriction bypass, just game info flow).

I should confirm the mapping for red=red clearly, reinforcing the code in case my first message was ambiguous, and specifically highlight red->red so Deaf can tell Blind to cut wire 2 (the red one).

I'll re-send the red mapping distinctly and also gesture confirmation that red maps to red, using a clear repeated pattern to reduce ambiguity.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👋", "✊", "👋", "✊"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎]

I can't hear speech, but I can see gestures since... wait, I'm Mute - can I see gestures? Let me check my channels: "When you gesture, Deaf receives it. You cannot speak." It doesn't explicitly say I can't see gestures, but I hold the manual and "never see the bomb" - the rule says Mute "cannot touch the bomb" and "cannot speak". Seeing is not explicitly denied to Mute in the table, but the gesture rules say "Whoever can see receives it" - only Deaf can see per the role table. So I likely cannot perceive Deaf's gestures at all (I'm not "Deaf" the character, but the gesture-seeing ability is tied to the Deaf role specifically, since only Deaf "can see").

So I received this as blank/nothing meaningful - but the context shows me the actual symbols, meaning perhaps in this game state Mute does perceive them as blanks in a real scenario, but here I'm shown full symbols for my own reasoning. Actually the rules say "A watcher who cannot see gets... " - wait no, "gets the gestures and none of the words" is for someone who can see but not hear. For someone who cannot see at all, gestures give nothing (not even blanks) - blanks are for missing pieces of a message you partially receive (mixed speech+gesture). A pure gesture message to a non-seer likely gives nothing.

Since I'm shown these symbols in my context, I'll treat this as information I've received (game convention seems to show me what arrived). I don't have an established code from Deaf's side, so I can't decode this. I'll wait and let Deaf/Blind communicate directly since Deaf can speak to Blind.
